title: [CRY-7] The shared epoch access key signs several structures with no domain separation; the SFU ad
description: Review finding CRY-7: The shared epoch access key signs several structures with no domain separation; the SFU admission proof is undefined and replayable (lens CRY). Location: spec/06-calls.md:111, spec/06-calls.md:119, spec/05-messaging.md:203, spec/05-messaging.md:206, spec/05-messaging.md:368. Fix: Split the finding. (a) The SFU proof is undefined (P2). 06:111 says the client "presents the MLS-membership access proof", and 06:119 says it "uses the epoch access proof (§5.2.2)". But §5.2.2 defines only envelope signatures, with no challenge, so whatever is presented is either a replayable gossiped envelope or an undefined signature over SFU-chosen bytes. Defining the proof as a signature over a context string, the SFU DID, a fresh SFU nonce and the `channelToken` closes both. This is a text gap, not something only the agora-pozi.8 external review can settle. (b) Domain separation (P3 on its own). No concrete cross-structure collision can be shown, because none of the signed structures has a defined encoding yet (see CRY-8). Distinct context prefixes are still the right fix and cost nothing once CRY-8 defines encodings. Full text: notes/review/CRY-verified.md and notes/review/CRY.md.
